claims.text: The proposed alloy has composition Al0.5Cr0.5CoFeNi.
The precursor uses elemental Al, Cr, Co, Fe, and Ni powders with purity above 99.9% and particle size below 25 µm.
Mechanical alloying produces a homogeneous precursor powder.
The alloy is consolidated by SPS at 1000 °C and 31.2 MPa for 15 minutes.
Rapid cooling is used after SPS.
Al0.5Cr0.5CoFeNi processed by the specified SPS route forms a mixed FCC/BCC microstructure.
The BCC phase fraction increases with Al content and reaches 32.9% at x=0.5.
The dual-phase microstructure at x=0.5 maximizes hardness.
The proposed composition and SPS treatment maximize density or produce density approaching the theoretical maximum.
Al0.5Cr0.5CoFeNi has superior corrosion resistance in 3.5 wt.% NaCl relative to lower-Al variants.
Maintaining the SPS temperature between 950 °C and 1050 °C prevents excessive grain growth and phase segregation.
Lattice distortion and high configurational entropy stabilize the Al0.5Cr0.5CoFeNi solid solution against phase separation.
High configurational entropy and lattice distortion suppress atomic diffusion during sintering.
Suppressed diffusion during SPS produces a fine-grained, dense microstructure.
Al at x=0.5 promotes a hard BCC phase that enhances hardness and strength.
The retained FCC phase and the Cr, Fe, and Ni distribution facilitate a stable passive oxide layer in chloride solution.
The proposed alloy has a Vickers hardness of approximately 412.6 HV.
The proposed alloy has a self-corrosion potential of 0.202 V in 3.5 wt.% NaCl.
Al0.1Cr0.9CoFeNi processed under the same SPS conditions is predominantly FCC.
The Al0.1Cr0.9CoFeNi baseline has a hardness of approximately 300 HV.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says the temperature must be strictly maintained between 950 and 1050 °C, whereas the boundary field says only that it must not exceed 1100 °C, leaving 1050–1100 °C inconsistently classified.

The predicted outcome assigns Ecorr = 0.202 V to x=0.5, while the baseline wording associates 0.202 V with a statement about the x=0.1 baseline and simultaneously says x<0.5 variants have lower values.
A hardness loss at 1150 °C due to grain coarsening is labeled falsifying, but it would support the stated prediction that temperatures above 1100 °C cause excessive grain growth.

Failure to densify or retain sufficient BCC phase at 900 °C is labeled falsifying even though 900 °C lies below the claimed valid processing range and would support the proposed lower-temperature boundary.

Lower hardness or corrosion resistance without mechanical alloying is labeled falsifying, but such a result would instead support the claim that mechanical alloying is critical to the proposed mechanism.
